copy.blurb:
Monday 15 June 2026 at 16:00 UTC. Spain and Cabo Verde on the card. On the the draw side, the engine's number sits +3.2pp clear of the market — a narrow gap this far out from kickoff.

Public Elo rates Spain 470 points higher than the other side (Spain 2010, Cabo Verde 1540). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Spain to win at 84%, the draw at 10%, and Cabo Verde to win at 6%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. the draw on the win side reads 10%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Spain to win at 89%, the draw at 7%, and Cabo Verde to win at 4%. The the draw side trades at 7% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +1371. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 10%, +3.2pp wider.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On the draw the lower bound is 10%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.2pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the the draw side specifically.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 24 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the the draw side still clears the Pick threshold.

copy.summary: The model and the market disagree on whether a stalemate is in play here. Our prior puts the draw at 10%; Polymarket prices it at 7%. The +3.2pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Spain v Cabo Verde · the model leans the draw
